inputs.about: URL for the repository's homepage.

inputs.name: auto_init
inputs.about: Create an initial commit with an empty README.

inputs.name: has_issues
inputs.about: Enable issues for this repository.

inputs.name: visibility
inputs.about: Repository visibility: 'public' (visible to everyone) or 'private' (visible to collaborators).

inputs.name: description
inputs.about: Short description of the repository.

inputs.name: is_template
inputs.about: Make this repository a template repository.

inputs.name: has_projects
inputs.about: Enable projects for this repository. Fails if organization has disabled repository projects and this is true.

inputs.name: has_downloads
inputs.about: Enable downloads for this repository (deprecated).

inputs.name: allow_auto_merge
inputs.about: Allow auto-merge on pull requests.

inputs.name: license_template
inputs.about: License template keyword (e.g., "mit", "apache-2.0"). See [GitHub license documentation](https://docs.github.com/articles/licensing-a-repository/#searching-github-by-license-type) for options.

inputs.name: custom_properties
inputs.about: JSON string containing custom properties for the repository as a key-value object. Example: '{"project_lead": "octocat", "status": "alpha"}'

inputs.name: allow_merge_commit
inputs.about: Allow merging pull requests with a merge commit.

inputs.name: allow_rebase_merge
inputs.about: Allow rebase-merging pull requests.

inputs.name: allow_squash_merge
inputs.about: Allow squash-merging pull requests.

inputs.name: gitignore_template
inputs.about: Name of the .gitignore template to apply (e.g., "Python", "Node"). Refer to the [GitHub gitignore template list](https://github.com/github/gitignore).

inputs.name: merge_commit_title
inputs.about: Default title for merge commits: 'PR_TITLE' or 'MERGE_MESSAGE'.

inputs.name: merge_commit_message
inputs.about: Default message for merge commits: 'PR_TITLE', 'PR_BODY', or 'BLANK'.

inputs.name: delete_branch_on_merge
inputs.about: Automatically delete head branches when pull requests are merged. Requires organization owner privileges if true.

inputs.name: squash_merge_commit_title
inputs.about: Default title for squash merge commits: 'PR_TITLE' or 'COMMIT_OR_PR_TITLE'.

inputs.name: squash_merge_commit_message
inputs.about: Default message for squash merge commits: 'PR_BODY', 'COMMIT_MESSAGES', or 'BLANK'.

inputs.name: use_squash_pr_title_as_default
inputs.about: DEPRECATED: Use `squash_merge_commit_title`. Default to pull request title for squash-merge commits.

tools.name: Create an organization variable
tools.description: Creates a new, uniquely named GitHub Actions variable for an organization, with configurable repository access visibility (all, private, or selected).

inputs.name: org
inputs.about: The name of the GitHub organization. This name is not case-sensitive.

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: The name of the organization variable. Must be unique at the organization level.

inputs.name: value
inputs.about: The value of the organization variable.

inputs.name: visibility
inputs.about: Controls which repositories in the organization can access the variable. Accepted values are 'all' (all repositories), 'private' (only private repositories), or 'selected' (specific repositories designated by `selected_repository_ids`).

inputs.name: selected_repository_ids
inputs.about: A list of repository integer IDs that can access this organization variable. This field is required and only applicable when `visibility` is set to 'selected'.

tools.name: Create an organization webhook
tools.description: Creates a webhook for a GitHub organization to deliver event notifications to a configured URL.

inputs.name: org
inputs.about: The name of the GitHub organization. This name is not case-sensitive.

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: The name of the webhook. Must be "web" for organization webhooks. Defaults to "web".

inputs.name: active
inputs.about: Boolean indicating if the webhook is active. `true` sends notifications, `false` does not. Defaults to `true`.

inputs.name: events
inputs.about: List of event names to trigger the webhook. Use `['*']` for all events. Defaults to `['push']` if not specified. See GitHub docs for event types.

inputs.name: config__url
inputs.about: Required. The target URL for webhook payload delivery. This URL is a mandatory part of the webhook's `config` object and will receive POST requests for subscribed events.

inputs.name: config__secret
inputs.about: Optional secret for generating an HMAC hex digest for payload verification (X-Hub-Signature-256 header). If provided, this is used as the key.

inputs.name: config__password
inputs.about: Password for basic authentication if the webhook endpoint (`config_url`) requires it, corresponding to `config_username`.

inputs.name: config__username
inputs.about: Username for basic authentication if the webhook endpoint (`config_url`) requires it. Use only if your endpoint is protected by basic auth.

inputs.name: config__content__type
inputs.about: The media type for serializing webhook payloads. Supported: `json`, `form`. GitHub API defaults to `form` if this field is not set or is `None`.

inputs.name: config__insecure__ssl
inputs.about: Controls SSL certificate verification for `config_url`. '1' disables verification (not recommended), '0' enables. GitHub API defaults to '0' (verification enabled) if this field is not set or is `None`.

tools.name: Create a project card
tools.description: Creates a card in a GitHub Projects (classic) column, either as a note or linked to an issue or pull request. DEPRECATED: The Projects (classic) REST API has been sunset, and Projects (classic) was removed from GitHub Enterprise Server 3.17. Use the newer GitHub Projects instead.

inputs.name: note
inputs.about: The text content for the card. Use this to create a note-only card. Either 'note' OR both 'content_id' and 'content_type' must be provided.

inputs.name: column_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the project column where the card will be created. This value is used as a path parameter in the API request URL (e.g., `/projects/columns/{column_id}/cards`).

inputs.name: content_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the issue or pull request to associate with this card. Required when content_type is specified. Get this from the issue/PR details (it's the numeric ID, not the issue number).

inputs.name: content_type
inputs.about: Type of content to associate with the card.

tools.name: Create a project column (Classic - Deprecated)
tools.description: Creates a named column in a GitHub Projects (classic) project to organize its cards. DEPRECATED: The Projects (classic) REST API has been sunset and this action no longer works on GitHub.com. Use GitHub Projects V2 with its GraphQL API instead.

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: The name for the new project column.

inputs.name: project_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the target GitHub project (classic) where the new column will be created.

tools.name: Create a pull request
tools.description: Creates a pull request in a GitHub repository, requiring existing `base` and `head` branches; `title` or `issue` must be provided.

inputs.name: base
inputs.about: The name of the branch you want the changes pulled into. This must be an existing branch on the current (target) repository. You cannot submit a pull request to one repository that requests a merge to a base branch of another repository.

inputs.name: body
inputs.about: The detailed description or contents of the pull request.

inputs.name: head
inputs.about: The name of the branch where your changes are implemented. IMPORTANT: This branch must already exist in the repository (or fork) before calling this action. You must first create the branch and push commits to it (using git or the 'Create a reference' action), then create the PR. For cross-repositor

inputs.name: repo
inputs.about: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This name is not case-sensitive.

inputs.name: draft
inputs.about: Indicates whether the pull request should be created as a draft. Draft pull requests cannot be merged until marked as ready for review.

inputs.name: issue
inputs.about: The number of an existing issue in the repository to convert into a pull request. If provided, the issue's title and body may be used for the pull request. Required if `title` is not specified.

inputs.name: owner
inputs.about: The account owner of the repository. This name is not case-sensitive.

inputs.name: title
inputs.about: The title of the new pull request. Required unless `issue` is specified.

inputs.name: head_repo
inputs.about: The name of the repository (e.g., 'octocat/Hello-World') where the changes in the pull request were made. This field is required for cross-repository pull requests if both the source and target repositories are owned by the same organization but are different repositories.

inputs.name: maintainer_can_modify
inputs.about: Indicates whether maintainers of the upstream repository can modify the pull request. This is primarily relevant for pull requests originating from forks.

tools.name: Create a reference
tools.description: Creates a NEW Git reference (branch or tag) in a repository. IMPORTANT: This action ONLY creates NEW references - if the reference already exists, it will fail with a 422 'Reference already exists' error. To update an existing reference, use the 'Update a reference' (GITHUB_UPDATE_A_REFERENCE) action instead. The repository must not be empty prior to this operation.

inputs.about: Fully qualified reference to create (e.g., `refs/heads/master`, `refs/tags/v1.0.0`). Must start with `refs/` and contain at least two slashes.

inputs.name: sha
inputs.about: SHA-1 hash of an existing commit in the repository that the new reference will point to.

inputs.name: repo
inputs.about: The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.

inputs.name: owner
inputs.about: The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.

tools.name: Create a registration token for an organization

inputs.name: org

inputs.about: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This field is not case-sensitive.

inputs.name: owner

tools.name: Create a release

inputs.name: draft
inputs.about: Set to `true` to create an unpublished (draft) release. Defaults to `false`.

inputs.name: owner
inputs.about: The account owner of the repository (username or organization name). This field is not case-sensitive.

inputs.name: discussion_category_name

inputs.name: repo

inputs.name: owner

tools.name: Create a reply for a review comment

inputs.name: allow_auto_merge
inputs.about: Whether to allow auto-merge on pull requests.

inputs.name: license_template
inputs.about: SPDX license key identifier (lowercase). Examples: 'mit', 'apache-2.0', 'gpl-3.0'. Must be one of the GitHub-supported licenses.

inputs.name: allow_merge_commit
inputs.about: Whether to allow merging pull requests with a merge commit.

inputs.name: allow_rebase_merge
inputs.about: Whether to allow rebase-merging pull requests.

inputs.name: allow_squash_merge
inputs.about: Whether to allow squash-merging pull requests.

inputs.name: gitignore_template
inputs.about: Desired .gitignore template (e.g., 'Python', 'Node').

inputs.name: merge_commit_title
inputs.about: The default title for a merge commit. `PR_TITLE` uses the pull request's title. `MERGE_MESSAGE` uses a classic title like 'Merge pull request #123 from branch-name'. Required when `merge_commit_message` is set. Valid combinations: (PR_TITLE, PR_BODY), (PR_TITLE, BLANK), (MERGE_MESSAGE, PR_TITLE).

inputs.name: merge_commit_message
inputs.about: The default message for a merge commit. `PR_BODY` uses the pull request's body. `PR_TITLE` uses the pull request's title. `BLANK` results in a blank commit message. Valid combinations with merge_commit_title: (PR_TITLE, PR_BODY), (PR_TITLE, BLANK), (MERGE_MESSAGE, PR_TITLE).

inputs.name: delete_branch_on_merge
inputs.about: Whether to automatically delete head branches when pull requests are merged.

inputs.name: squash_merge_commit_title
inputs.about: The default title for a squash merge commit. `PR_TITLE` uses the pull request's title. `COMMIT_OR_PR_TITLE` uses the commit's title (if only one commit) or the pull request's title (if multiple commits).

inputs.name: squash_merge_commit_message
inputs.about: The default message for a squash merge commit. `PR_BODY` uses the pull request's body. `COMMIT_MESSAGES` uses the branch's commit messages. `BLANK` results in a blank commit message.

tools.name: Create a repository from an unpublished codespace
tools.description: Publishes the specified codespace to a new repository, using the codespace's current state as the initial commit.

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: The desired name for the new repository to be created from the codespace. If omitted, GitHub might generate a name (e.g., based on the codespace name).

inputs.name: private
inputs.about: Specifies the visibility of the new repository. Set to `true` for a private repository, or `false` for a public one. Defaults to `false` (public).

inputs.name: codespace_name
inputs.about: The unique name of the codespace to be published as a new repository. This codespace must exist, be unpublished, and belong to the authenticated user.

tools.name: Create a repository project
tools.description: Creates a GitHub Projects V2 project owned by the repository owner and linked to the specified repository. A supplied project description is not applied during creation.

inputs.name: body
inputs.about: An optional detailed description for the project board. Note: GitHub Projects V2 does not support a body/description field during creation, so this field is accepted but not used.

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: The name of the project board to be created.

inputs.name: repo
inputs.about: The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.

inputs.name: owner
inputs.about: The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.

tools.name: Create a repository ruleset
tools.description: Creates a uniquely named ruleset for a repository, defining rules for branches or tags with specified enforcement, conditions, and bypass actors.

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: Unique name for the ruleset.

inputs.name: repo
inputs.about: Name of the repository, without the `.git` extension (not case-sensitive).

inputs.name: owner
inputs.about: Account owner of the repository (not case-sensitive).

inputs.name: rules
inputs.about: Array of rule objects as a JSON string to be enforced. Each must have `type` and may have `parameters`. Refer to GitHub API docs for available rule types and parameters. Example: '[{"type": "creation"}, {"type": "deletion"}]'

inputs.name: target
inputs.about: The target of the ruleset, whether it applies to branches or tags.

inputs.name: enforcement
inputs.about: Enforcement level: `disabled` (ruleset is not enforced), `active` (ruleset is enforced), or `evaluate` (test rules before enforcing; GitHub Enterprise only).

inputs.name: bypass_actors
inputs.about: Actors that can bypass rules in this ruleset as a JSON string. Each actor object requires `actor_id`, `actor_type` (e.g., 'Team', 'Integration'), and `bypass_mode` (e.g., 'always'). Example: '[{"actor_id": 1, "actor_type": "Team", "bypass_mode": "always"}]'

inputs.name: conditions__ref__name__exclude
inputs.about: Ref names or patterns to exclude. Condition fails if any pattern matches the ref name.

inputs.name: conditions__ref__name__include
inputs.about: Ref names/patterns to include. Condition passes if one pattern matches the ref name. Use `~DEFAULT_BRANCH` for default branch, `~ALL` for all branches.

tools.name: Create a repository using a template
tools.description: Creates a new repository from an existing template repository; the authenticated user must have access to the template and, if creating in an organization, repository creation permissions within it.

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: The desired name for the new repository to be created.

inputs.name: owner
inputs.about: The username or organization name that will own the new repository. Defaults to the authenticated user if not provided.

inputs.name: private
inputs.about: Set to `true` to create a private repository, or `false` to create a public repository.

inputs.name: description
inputs.about: A brief summary or description for the new repository.

inputs.name: template_repo
inputs.about: The name of the template repository, without the `.git` extension. This field is not case-sensitive.

inputs.name: template_owner
inputs.about: The username or organization name that owns the template repository. This field is not case-sensitive.

inputs.name: include_all_branches
inputs.about: Set to `true` to copy the directory structure and files from all branches of the template repository, not just the default branch.

tools.name: Create a repository variable
tools.description: Creates a new, unencrypted variable in a repository for GitHub Actions workflows; fails if a variable with the same name already exists.

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: The name of the variable to create. Variable names are case-sensitive and can only contain alphanumeric characters ([a-z], [A-Z], [0-9]) or underscores (_). They cannot start with the `GITHUB_` prefix, and spaces are not allowed.

inputs.name: repo
inputs.about: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This field is not case sensitive.

inputs.name: owner
inputs.about: The username or organization name that owns the repository. This field is not case sensitive.

inputs.name: value
inputs.about: The value of the variable. This will be stored as a string.

tools.name: Create a repository webhook
tools.description: Creates a webhook for a specified repository; requires admin permissions on the repository.

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: Name of the webhook. Use `web`. This parameter currently only accepts `web` and defaults to `web` if not provided.

inputs.name: repo
inputs.about: The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. This name is not case sensitive.

inputs.name: owner
inputs.about: The account owner of the repository. This name is not case sensitive.

inputs.name: active
inputs.about: Determines if notifications are sent when the webhook is triggered. `true` sends notifications (active), `false` disables them (inactive).

inputs.name: events
inputs.about: List of events to trigger the webhook (e.g., `['push']`, `['issues']`). See GitHub documentation for 'webhook event payloads'.

inputs.name: config__url
inputs.about: The URL to which webhook payloads will be delivered via POST for subscribed events.

inputs.name: config__secret
inputs.about: Optional secret string for HMAC hex digest in delivery signature headers, enhancing security. See GitHub's 'delivery signature headers' documentation for details.

inputs.name: config__content__type
inputs.about: Media type for serializing payloads: `json` or `form`. Defaults to `form` if not specified. `json` delivers JSON, `form` delivers URL-encoded data.

inputs.name: config__insecure__ssl
inputs.about: Determines SSL certificate verification for the payload URL: "0" to verify SSL (recommended), or "1" to skip. Defaults to "0" (verify SSL) if not provided.

tools.name: Create a review comment for a pull request
tools.description: Creates a review comment on a pull request diff at a specific line or range, using a diff position, or as a reply to an existing review comment.

inputs.name: body
inputs.about: Text content of the review comment.

inputs.name: line
inputs.about: **[LINE-BASED MODE]** Line number in the diff for the comment. Required when using line-based mode (must be used with `side`). For multi-line comments, this is the last line of the range. Do not use with position or in_reply_to parameters.

inputs.name: path
inputs.about: Relative path of the file for the comment.

inputs.name: repo
inputs.about: Repository name without the `.git` extension (not case sensitive).

inputs.name: side
inputs.about: **[LINE-BASED MODE]** Side of the diff (`LEFT` or `RIGHT`) for the comment. Required when using line-based mode with the `line` parameter. For multi-line comments, refers to the last line of the range. Do not use with position or in_reply_to parameters. **IMPORTANT:** Use `LEFT` only for deletions t

inputs.name: owner
inputs.about: Account owner of the repository (not case sensitive).

inputs.name: position
inputs.about: **[DEPRECATED - Use line-based mode instead]** Position in the diff hunk for the comment. When using position mode, do not provide line, side, start_line, start_side, or in_reply_to parameters.

inputs.name: commit_id
inputs.about: SHA of the commit for the comment. Using an outdated `commit_id` can misplace the comment if lines change.

inputs.name: start_line
inputs.about: **[LINE-BASED MODE - MULTI-LINE]** First line in the diff for a multi-line comment. Required when creating a multi-line comment (must be used with `start_side`, `line`, and `side`). Do not use with position or in_reply_to parameters.

inputs.name: start_side
inputs.about: **[LINE-BASED MODE - MULTI-LINE]** Starting side of the diff (`LEFT` or `RIGHT`) for a multi-line comment. Required when creating a multi-line comment (must be used with `start_line`, `line`, and `side`). Do not use with position or in_reply_to parameters. **IMPORTANT:** Use `LEFT` only for deletion

inputs.name: in_reply_to
inputs.about: **[REPLY MODE]** ID of an existing review comment to reply to. When using reply mode, do not provide position, line, side, start_line, or start_side parameters as they will be ignored.

inputs.name: pull_number
inputs.about: Identifier of the pull request.

tools.name: Create a review for a pull request
tools.description: Creates a pull request review, allowing approval, change requests, or comments; `body` is required if `event` is `REQUEST_CHANGES` or `COMMENT`, and omitting `event` makes the review `PENDING`.

inputs.name: body
inputs.about: Review's main body text; required if `event` is `REQUEST_CHANGES` or `COMMENT`.

inputs.name: repo
inputs.about: Repository name, without the `.git` extension (case-insensitive).

inputs.name: event
inputs.about: Review action type (`APPROVE`, `REQUEST_CHANGES`, `COMMENT`); if omitted, review is `PENDING` and requires later submission.

inputs.name: owner
inputs.about: Username of the account owning the repository (case-insensitive).

inputs.name: comments
inputs.about: Inline draft review comments. Each object requires `path` (relative file path) and `body` (comment text). Optionally, specify `line` (or `start_line` for multi-line), and `side` (or `start_side`) for diff location. `position` is deprecated; use `line`. Example: `[{'path': 'file.py', 'line': 10, 'bod

inputs.name: commit_id
inputs.about: SHA of the commit to review; defaults to the latest pull request commit. Outdated SHAs may lead to stale comments.

inputs.name: pull_number
inputs.about: Identifying number of the pull request.

tools.name: Create a scoped access token
tools.description: Creates a repository-scoped and/or permission-scoped GitHub App user access token from a non-scoped user token. The endpoint requires Basic authentication with the app's client ID and client secret; repository scope may be specified by names or IDs.

inputs.name: target
inputs.about: Username or organization name for scoping the new token. Required if `target_id` is not provided.

inputs.name: client_id
inputs.about: Client ID of the GitHub App.

inputs.name: target_id
inputs.about: ID of the user or organization for scoping the new token. Required if `target` is not provided.

inputs.name: access_token
inputs.about: User-to-server access token to be exchanged for a new scoped token.

inputs.name: repositories
inputs.about: Repository names to scope the new token to. Cannot be used if `repository_ids` is specified.

inputs.name: repository_ids
inputs.about: Repository IDs to scope the new token to. Cannot be used if `repositories` is specified.

inputs.name: permissions__pages
inputs.about: Permission for GitHub Pages settings, statuses, configurations, builds, and creating new builds. Applies to target repositories.

inputs.name: permissions__checks
inputs.about: Permission for checks on code (e.g., CI statuses). Applies to target repositories.

inputs.name: permissions__issues
inputs.about: Permission for issues, comments, assignees, labels, and milestones. Applies to target repositories.

inputs.name: permissions__actions
inputs.about: Permission for GitHub Actions workflows, workflow runs, and artifacts. Applies to target repositories.

inputs.name: permissions__members
inputs.about: Permission for organization members and teams. Applies to target organization.

inputs.name: permissions__profile
inputs.about: Permission to manage profile settings for the user account. Applies to target user.

inputs.name: permissions__secrets
inputs.about: Permission for repository secrets (e.g., Actions secrets). Applies to target repositories.

inputs.name: permissions__contents
inputs.about: Permission for repository contents, commits, branches, downloads, releases, and merges. Applies to target repositories.

inputs.name: permissions__metadata
inputs.about: Read-only permission for repository metadata, search, and collaborator listing. Applies to target repositories.

inputs.name: permissions__packages
inputs.about: Permission for packages in GitHub Packages. Applies to target repositories or organization.

inputs.name: permissions__starring
inputs.about: Permission to list and manage repositories a user is starring. Applies to target user.

inputs.name: permissions__statuses
inputs.about: Permission for commit statuses. Applies to target repositories.

inputs.name: permissions__followers
inputs.about: Permission to manage followers for the user account. Applies to target user.

inputs.name: permissions__gpg__keys
inputs.about: Permission to view and manage GPG keys for the user account. Applies to target user.

inputs.name: permissions__workflows
inputs.about: Permission for updating GitHub Actions workflow files. Requires `contents: write`. Applies to target repositories.

inputs.name: permissions__codespaces
inputs.about: Permission for Codespaces. Applies to target user/organization if repositories are not specified, otherwise to target repositories.

inputs.name: permissions__deployments
inputs.about: Permission for deployments and deployment statuses. Applies to target repositories.

inputs.name: permissions__environments
inputs.about: Permission for repository environments. Applies to target repositories.

inputs.name: permissions__single__file
inputs.about: Permission to access specific files in targeted repositories. The file paths must be configured in the GitHub App settings.

inputs.name: permissions__administration
inputs.about: Permission for repository administration (settings, teams, collaborators). Applies to target repositories.

inputs.name: permissions__git__ssh__keys
inputs.about: Permission to manage Git SSH keys for the user account. Applies to target user.

inputs.name: permissions__pull__requests
inputs.about: Permission for pull requests, comments, assignees, labels, milestones, and merges. Applies to target repositories.

inputs.name: permissions__email__addresses
inputs.about: Permission to manage email addresses for the user account. Applies to target user.

inputs.name: permissions__security__events
inputs.about: Permission for security events (e.g., code scanning alerts). Applies to target repositories.

inputs.name: permissions__repository__hooks
inputs.about: Permission for repository webhooks. Applies to target repositories.

inputs.name: permissions__team__discussions
inputs.about: Permission for team discussions and related comments. Applies to target organization.

inputs.name: permissions__organization__plan
inputs.about: Read-only permission for viewing an organization's billing plan. Applies to target organization.

inputs.name: permissions__dependabot__secrets
inputs.about: Permission for Dependabot secrets for targeted repositories.

inputs.name: permissions__interaction__limits
inputs.about: Permission to view and manage interaction limits on a repository. Applies to target repositories or organization.

inputs.name: permissions__organization__hooks
inputs.about: Permission for organization webhooks. Applies to target organization.

inputs.name: permissions__organization__events
inputs.about: Read-only permission to view organization audit log events. Applies to target organization.

inputs.name: permissions__repository__projects
inputs.about: Permission for repository projects, columns, and cards. Applies to target repositories.

inputs.name: permissions__organization__secrets
inputs.about: Permission for organization-level secrets (e.g., Actions secrets). Applies to target organization.

inputs.name: permissions__vulnerability__alerts
inputs.about: Permission for Dependabot alerts. Applies to target repositories.

inputs.name: permissions__organization__packages
inputs.about: Permission for organization-level GitHub Packages. Applies to target organization.

inputs.name: permissions__organization__projects
inputs.about: Permission for organization projects and projects beta (if available). Applies to target organization.

inputs.name: permissions__secret__scanning__alerts
inputs.about: Permission for secret scanning alerts. Applies to target repositories.

inputs.name: permissions__organization__custom__roles
inputs.about: Permission for custom repository roles within an organization. Applies to target organization.

inputs.name: permissions__organization__administration
inputs.about: Permission for administrative settings of an organization. Applies to target organization.

inputs.name: permissions__organization__user__blocking
inputs.about: Permission for viewing and managing users blocked by the organization. Applies to target organization.

inputs.name: permissions__repository__custom__properties
inputs.about: Permission to view and edit repository custom properties, if allowed by property definition. Applies to target repositories.

inputs.name: permissions__organization__custom__org__roles
inputs.about: Permission for custom organization roles. Applies to target organization.

inputs.name: permissions__organization__custom__properties
inputs.about: Permission for custom properties for an organization. Applies to target organization.

inputs.name: permissions__organization__announcement__banners
inputs.about: Permission to view and manage organization announcement banners. Applies to target organization.

inputs.name: permissions__organization__self__hosted__runners
inputs.about: Permission for GitHub Actions self-hosted runners for an organization. Applies to target organization.

inputs.name: permissions__organization__personal__access__tokens
inputs.about: Permission for fine-grained personal access tokens requested by organization members. Applies to target organization.

inputs.name: permissions__organization__copilot__seat__management
inputs.about: Permission for GitHub Copilot seat assignments for organization members (beta). Applies to target organization.

inputs.name: permissions__organization__personal__access__token__requests
inputs.about: Permission for requests for fine-grained personal access tokens within an organization. Applies to target organization.

tools.name: Create a dependency snapshot
tools.description: Creates a snapshot of a repository's dependencies to populate the GitHub dependency graph and enable security alerts; `sha` must be a 40-character commit ID, `ref` a fully qualified Git reference (e.g., `refs/heads/main`), and `scanned` an ISO 8601 timestamp.

inputs.name: ref
inputs.about: Git reference (fully qualified, e.g., `refs/heads/main`) of the repository branch/tag that triggered this snapshot.

inputs.name: sha
inputs.about: Commit SHA (maximum 40 characters) associated with this dependency snapshot.

inputs.name: repo
inputs.about: Repository name, without `.git` extension (name is not case-sensitive).

inputs.name: owner
inputs.about: Account owner of the repository (name is not case-sensitive).

inputs.name: job__id
inputs.about: Optional external ID of the job that generated this snapshot.

inputs.name: scanned
inputs.about: UTC timestamp (ISO 8601 format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ) when the snapshot was taken.

inputs.name: version
inputs.about: Version of the dependency snapshot submission, typically of the manifest or lock file format.

inputs.name: metadata
inputs.about: Optional user-defined metadata as a JSON string for domain-specific information. Limited to 8 keys with scalar values (e.g., string, number, boolean). Example: '{"key1": "value1", "key2": 123}'

inputs.name: manifests
inputs.about: Optional collection of package manifests as a JSON string (e.g., package-lock.json, pom.xml). Keys are manifest file names; values detail dependencies. Example: '{"package-lock.json": {"name": "...", "resolved": {...}}}'

inputs.name: detector__url
inputs.about: Optional URL of the detector tool used.

inputs.name: detector__name
inputs.about: Optional name of the tool used to detect dependencies.

inputs.name: job__html__url
inputs.about: Optional URL for the job that generated this snapshot.

inputs.name: job__correlator
inputs.about: Optional string to group snapshots. For a given `job.correlator` and `detector.name`, only the 'latest' snapshot is current. Useful to distinguish detection runs (e.g., concatenating GITHUB_WORKFLOW and GITHUB_JOB).

inputs.name: detector__version
inputs.about: Optional version of the detector tool used.

tools.name: Create a tag object
tools.description: Creates an annotated Git tag object in a repository, pointing to an existing commit, tree, or blob identified by its SHA and specified type.

inputs.name: tag
inputs.about: The name of the tag, typically a version identifier (e.g., "v0.0.1").

inputs.name: repo
inputs.about: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This name is not case-sensitive.

inputs.name: type
inputs.about: The type of the Git object being tagged.

inputs.name: owner
inputs.about: The account owner of the repository. This name is not case-sensitive.

inputs.name: object
inputs.about: The SHA of the Git object (commit, tree, or blob) that this tag is pointing to.

inputs.name: message
inputs.about: The message associated with the tag.

inputs.name: tagger__date
inputs.about: The timestamp for when this object was tagged. This should be in ISO 8601 format: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`.

inputs.name: tagger__name
inputs.about: The name of the person creating the tag.

inputs.name: tagger__email
inputs.about: The email address of the person creating the tag.

tools.name: Create a tag protection state for a repository
tools.description: Creates a legacy tag protection rule for a repository, using a glob pattern to select protected tags. DEPRECATED: GitHub sunset the tag protection API on GitHub.com and says it returns null data; use GITHUB_CREATE_A_REPOSITORY_RULESET to protect tags with repository rulesets instead.

inputs.name: repo
inputs.about: The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. Not case sensitive.

inputs.name: owner
inputs.about: The account owner of the repository (username or organization name). Not case sensitive.

inputs.name: pattern
inputs.about: Glob pattern to protect tags. Examples: `v1.*` (protects tags starting with `v1.`), `*` (protects all tags).

tools.name: Create a team
tools.description: Creates a new team in an organization, optionally with maintainers, repositories, specific privacy, notification settings, or a parent team; if `parent_team_id` is given, `privacy` must be 'closed'.

inputs.name: org
inputs.about: Organization name where the team will be created (not case-sensitive).

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: Name of the new team.

inputs.name: privacy
inputs.about: Team privacy: 'secret' (visible to owners and members) or 'closed' (visible to all org members). Defaults to 'secret' for non-nested teams; must be 'closed' if `parent_team_id` is set.

inputs.name: permission
inputs.about: **Deprecated**. Default repository permission ('pull' for read access, 'push' for write access) for the team.

inputs.name: repo_names
inputs.about: Repository full names (e.g., "org-name/repo-name") for team access; repositories must exist and be accessible to the organization.

inputs.name: description
inputs.about: Team's purpose or focus.

inputs.name: maintainers
inputs.about: GitHub user handles of organization members to be team maintainers; users must be organization members.

inputs.name: parent_team_id
inputs.about: ID of an existing team to be the parent, creating a nested team. If provided, new team `privacy` must be 'closed'.

inputs.name: notification_setting
inputs.about: Notification settings for @mentions: 'notifications_enabled' (members notified) or 'notifications_disabled' (no one notified). Default: 'notifications_enabled'.

tools.name: Create a temporary private fork
tools.description: Creates a temporary private fork of the specified repository to address a security vulnerability, linking the fork to a GHSA ID that must be specifically associated with this repository; the fork may take up to 5 minutes to become accessible.

inputs.name: repo
inputs.about: Name of the repository, without the `.git` extension; not case-sensitive.

inputs.name: owner
inputs.about: Account owner (username or organization) of the repository; not case-sensitive.

inputs.name: ghsa_id
inputs.about: Identifier for the GitHub Security Advisory (e.g., GHSA-rfv9-x7w6-39px) that the fork will address.

tools.name: Create a tree
tools.description: Creates a new Git tree object in a repository, defining file/directory structure by specifying tree entries, optionally building on a `base_tree` SHA; all provided SHAs must be valid.

inputs.name: repo
inputs.about: The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.

inputs.name: tree
inputs.about: Array of objects defining the tree structure. Each object (node) requires `path` (string), `mode` (string; e.g., '100644' file, '100755' executable, '040000' subdirectory/tree, '160000' submodule, '120000' symlink), and `type` (string: 'blob', 'tree', or 'commit'). For new/updated blobs, provide `co

inputs.name: owner
inputs.about: The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.

inputs.name: base_tree
inputs.about: SHA1 of an existing Git tree object to use as a base. If provided, its entries are combined with `tree` entries, where `tree` entries overwrite those from `base_tree` with the same path. Typically the SHA1 of the latest commit's tree for new branch changes. If omitted, the new tree is built from `tr

tools.name: Create a user project
tools.description: Creates a GitHub Projects V2 project board for the authenticated user using the GraphQL API. An optional project description is accepted but not applied during creation.

inputs.name: body
inputs.about: Optional description for the new project. Note: GitHub Projects V2 does not support a body/description field during creation, so this field is accepted but not used.

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: Name/title for the new project. This will be displayed as the project board title.

tools.name: Create a workflow dispatch event
tools.description: Manually triggers a GitHub Actions workflow identified by `workflow_id` at a given `ref`, if the workflow is configured to accept `workflow_dispatch` events.

inputs.name: ref
inputs.about: Git reference (branch or tag) for the workflow.

inputs.name: repo
inputs.about: Repository name, excluding the `.git` extension (case-insensitive).

inputs.name: owner
inputs.about: Owner of the repository (username or organization, case-insensitive).

inputs.name: inputs
inputs.about: JSON string containing key-value inputs for the workflow, matching `on.workflow_dispatch.inputs` definitions (max 10); uses workflow defaults if omitted. Example: '{"actor": "mona", "environment": "production"}'

inputs.name: workflow_id
inputs.about: Identifier of the workflow: numeric ID or just the filename (e.g., 'main.yml'). If a full path like '.github/workflows/main.yml' is provided, the prefix is automatically stripped.

tools.name: Create a branch
tools.description: Creates a new branch in a GitHub repository pointing to a specified commit. Use this action when you need to create a new branch from an existing commit SHA. IMPORTANT: This action only creates NEW branches. If the branch already exists, it will fail with a 422 'Reference already exists' error. The repository must not be empty (must have at least one commit) before creating a branch.

inputs.name: sha
inputs.about: The SHA-1 hash of the commit that the new branch will point to. This must be an existing commit in the repository (40-character hexadecimal string).

inputs.name: repo
inputs.about: The name of the repository without the .git extension. This field is not case-sensitive.

inputs.name: owner
inputs.about: The account owner of the repository (username or organization name). This field is not case-sensitive.

inputs.name: branch_name
inputs.about: The name of the new branch to create (e.g., 'feature-branch', 'fix-bug-123'). Do not include 'refs/heads/' prefix - just provide the branch name.

tools.name: Create commit signature protection
tools.description: Enables commit signature protection for a specified branch, requiring all new commits to be signed.

inputs.name: repo
inputs.about: The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.

inputs.name: owner
inputs.about: The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.

inputs.name: branch
inputs.about: The name of the branch. Cannot contain wildcard characters. To use wildcard characters in branch names, use [the GraphQL API](https://docs.github.com/graphql).

tools.name: Create a custom deployment protection rule on an environment
tools.description: Enables a custom deployment protection rule for an existing environment in a repository by linking a configured GitHub App (via `integration_id`) to control deployments.

inputs.name: repo
inputs.about: The name of the repository where the environment exists. Do not include the `.git` extension. This name is not case sensitive.

inputs.name: owner
inputs.about: The GitHub username or organization name that owns the repository. This name is not case sensitive.

inputs.name: integration_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the GitHub App that provides the custom deployment protection rule. This app must be installed and configured for the repository. Required - use GITHUB_LIST_ENVIRONMENT_CUSTOM_DEPLOYMENT_RULES to find available integration IDs for your environment.

inputs.name: environment_name
inputs.about: The name of the environment to which the protection rule will be applied. This name must be URL-encoded if it contains special characters (e.g., slashes `/` should be replaced with `%2F`).

tools.name: Create draft item for user project
tools.description: Creates a draft issue item in a user-owned GitHub ProjectsV2. Use when you need to add a new draft item to track ideas or tasks in a user's project.

inputs.name: body
inputs.about: The body content of the draft issue item to create in the project.

inputs.name: title
inputs.about: The title of the draft issue item to create in the project.

inputs.name: username
inputs.about: The handle for the GitHub user account.

inputs.name: project_number
inputs.about: The project's number.

tools.name: Create inference chat completions
tools.description: Tool to create chat completions using GitHub Models inference API. Use when you need to generate AI-powered text responses using models like GPT-4, Claude, or Llama through GitHub's inference endpoint.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.about: If specified, the system will make a best effort to sample deterministically, such that repeated requests with the same seed and parameters should return the same result.

inputs.name: stop
inputs.about: Up to 4 sequences where the API will stop generating further tokens. The returned text will not contain the stop sequence.

inputs.name: model
inputs.about: ID of the specific model to use for the request. Format: {publisher}/{model_name}, e.g., openai/gpt-4o, anthropic/claude-3.5-sonnet.

inputs.name: tools
inputs.about: A list of tools (functions) the model may call. The model will choose when and how to call these functions based on the conversation context.

inputs.name: top_p
inputs.about: An alternative to temperature called nucleus sampling. Range: [0.0, 1.0]. The model considers tokens with top_p probability mass.

inputs.name: stream
inputs.about: If true, partial message deltas will be sent as data-only server-sent events as they become available.

inputs.name: messages
inputs.about: The collection of context messages associated with this chat completion request. Each message must have a role (assistant, developer, system, or user) and content.

inputs.name: max_tokens
inputs.about: Maximum number of tokens to generate in the completion. The total length of input tokens and generated tokens is limited by the model's context length.

inputs.name: modalities
inputs.about: List of supported modalities for this request. Supported values: text, audio.

inputs.name: temperature
inputs.about: Controls the apparent creativity of generated completions. Range: [0.0, 1.0]. Lower values make output more deterministic, higher values more random.

inputs.name: tool_choice
inputs.about: Controls which (if any) tool is called by the model.

inputs.name: stream_options
inputs.about: Options for streaming responses.

inputs.name: response_format
inputs.about: Specifies the format of the model's output.

inputs.name: presence_penalty
inputs.about: Influences probability of generated tokens appearing based on whether they appear in the text so far. Range: [-2.0, 2.0]. Positive values increase likelihood of new topics.

inputs.name: frequency_penalty
inputs.about: Influences probability of generated tokens appearing based on their cumulative frequency in the text so far. Range: [-2.0, 2.0]. Positive values decrease likelihood of repetition.

tools.name: Create inference embeddings
tools.description: Tool to create inference embeddings using GitHub's AI models. Use when you need to convert text into vector representations for similarity search, clustering, or other ML tasks.

inputs.name: user
inputs.about: A unique identifier representing your end-user, which can help monitor and detect abuse.

inputs.name: input
inputs.about: Input text to embed, encoded as a string or array of strings. Each string will be converted to an embedding vector.

inputs.name: model
inputs.about: ID of the specific model to use for the request. Format: {publisher}/{model_name}

inputs.name: dimensions
inputs.about: The number of dimensions the resulting output embeddings should have. Must be supported by the model (max 2048).

inputs.name: encoding_format
inputs.about: Format for embeddings: 'float' (default) or 'base64'. Float returns arrays of numbers, base64 returns encoded strings.

tools.name: Create issue type
tools.description: Create a new issue type for a GitHub organization. Requires the authenticated user to be an organization administrator. OAuth tokens need admin:org scope.

inputs.name: org
inputs.about: The organization name (case-insensitive).

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: The name of the issue type.

inputs.name: color
inputs.about: The color of the issue type.

inputs.name: is_enabled
inputs.about: Whether the issue type is enabled at the organization level.

inputs.name: description
inputs.about: A short description of the issue type.

tools.name: Create JIT runner config for repo
tools.description: Generates a temporary Just-In-Time (JIT) configuration for a new self-hosted GitHub Actions runner for a repository; any specified non-default `runner_group_id` must be an existing runner group accessible by the repository.

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: The desired name for the new self-hosted runner.

inputs.name: repo
inputs.about: The name of the repository, without the '.git' extension. This field is not case-sensitive.

inputs.name: owner
inputs.about: The username or organization name that owns the repository. This field is not case-sensitive.

inputs.name: labels
inputs.about: A list of custom labels to assign to the runner. These labels help in targeting specific runners for jobs. Minimum items: 1. Maximum items: 100.

inputs.name: work_folder
inputs.about: The working directory for the runner, relative to its installation path. This is where job execution will take place.

inputs.name: runner_group_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the runner group to which the new runner will be assigned. Use 0 for the default group or the ID of a specific runner group.

tools.name: Create or update an environment
tools.description: Creates a new environment or updates an existing one in a GitHub repository, allowing configuration of deployment protection rules such as wait timers and reviewers; ensure `environment_name` is URL-encoded if it contains special characters.

inputs.name: repo
inputs.about: Name of the repository, without the `.git` extension (not case-sensitive).

inputs.name: owner
inputs.about: The username or organization name of the repository owner (not case-sensitive).

inputs.name: reviewers
inputs.about: JSON string containing up to 6 users or teams allowed to review deployments. Reviewers need at least read access; one approval suffices. Each reviewer object requires `id` and `type` ('User' or 'Team'). Example: '[{"id": 4532, "type": "User"}]'

inputs.name: wait_timer
inputs.about: Time in minutes to delay a job after it's triggered (0-43,200, i.e., up to 30 days).

inputs.name: environment_name
inputs.about: Name of the environment. URL-encode if it contains special characters (e.g., '/' becomes '%2F').

inputs.name: prevent_self_review
inputs.about: If true, prevents the user who triggered deployment from approving their own job.

inputs.name: deployment__branch__policy__protected__branches
inputs.about: If true, only branches with existing protection rules can deploy; `deployment_branch_policy_custom_branch_policies` must then be false.

inputs.name: deployment__branch__policy__custom__branch__policies
inputs.about: If true, deployment is restricted to branches matching custom name patterns; `deployment_branch_policy_protected_branches` must then be false.

tools.name: Create or update an environment secret
tools.description: Creates or updates an environment secret with an `encrypted_value` that was encrypted using the public key identified by `key_id` for the specified environment.

inputs.name: repo
inputs.about: The name of the repository. Not case-sensitive.

inputs.name: owner
inputs.about: The account owner of the repository. Not case-sensitive.

inputs.name: key_id
inputs.about: ID of the public key used for encryption, obtained from the 'Get an environment public key' GitHub API endpoint.

inputs.name: secret_name
inputs.about: Name of the secret. Case-sensitive.

inputs.name: encrypted_value
inputs.about: Value of the secret, encrypted with LibSodium using the public key obtained from the 'Get an environment public key' GitHub API endpoint for the target environment.

inputs.name: environment_name
inputs.about: Name of the environment. Case-sensitive; URL-encode special characters (e.g., `/` becomes `%2F`).

tools.name: Create or update an organization secret
tools.description: Creates or updates an organization secret for GitHub Actions, requiring its value to be pre-encrypted via LibSodium using the organization's public key.

inputs.name: org
inputs.about: The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.

inputs.name: key_id
inputs.about: ID of the public key (from 'Get an organization public key' endpoint) used for encryption. This is required for both creating and updating secrets.

inputs.name: visibility
inputs.about: Controls which repositories can access the secret. If 'selected', `selected_repository_ids` must be provided.

inputs.name: secret_name
inputs.about: The name of the secret.

inputs.name: encrypted_value
inputs.about: Value for the secret, pre-encrypted using LibSodium with the organization's public key (obtained from 'Get an organization public key' endpoint). This is required for both creating and updating secrets.

inputs.name: selected_repository_ids
inputs.about: List of repository IDs that can access this secret. Required and only applicable when `visibility` is 'selected'.

tools.name: Create or update a repository secret
tools.description: Creates or updates a GitHub Actions secret within a specific repository; use `encrypted_value` and `key_id` to set or change its value.

inputs.name: repo
inputs.about: The repository name, without the `.git` extension (case-insensitive).

inputs.name: owner
inputs.about: The repository owner's username or organization name (case-insensitive).

inputs.name: key_id
inputs.about: ID of the public key used to encrypt `encrypted_value` (obtained with the public key). Required if `encrypted_value` is provided.

inputs.name: secret_name
inputs.about: The name for the secret being created or updated. Must not start with 'GITHUB_' prefix (reserved for GitHub internal secrets).

inputs.name: encrypted_value
inputs.about: Value for the secret, pre-encrypted with the repository's public key using LibSodium (public key is obtained via 'Get a repository public key' endpoint).

tools.name: Create or update a secret for the authenticated user
tools.description: Creates or updates a Codespaces secret for the authenticated user, optionally restricting access to selected repositories. Accepts plaintext and encrypts it using the user's GitHub public key, or accepts a pre-encrypted value with its key ID.

inputs.name: key_id
inputs.about: ID of the public key (from GitHub's 'Get public key for the authenticated user' endpoint) used to encrypt `encrypted_value`. If not provided, it will be fetched automatically.

inputs.name: secret_name
inputs.about: The name of the secret. This name must be unique among the user's Codespaces secrets.

inputs.name: secret_value
inputs.about: The plaintext value for your secret. This will be automatically encrypted using the user's Codespaces public key before being sent to GitHub. If you already have an encrypted value, use the encrypted_value parameter instead.

inputs.name: encrypted_value
inputs.about: Secret's value, encrypted using [LibSodium](https://libsodium.gitbook.io/doc/bindings_for_other_languages) with the public key (see `key_id`) obtained from GitHub's 'Get public key for the authenticated user' endpoint.

inputs.name: selected_repository_ids
inputs.about: Repository IDs that can access this secret. If omitted or empty, accessible to all user's Codespaces-enabled repositories.

tools.name: Create or update custom properties for an organization
tools.description: Creates new custom property schemas or updates existing ones in bulk for a specified organization; each property definition must include `property_name` and `value_type`.

inputs.name: org
inputs.about: The case-insensitive organization name.

inputs.name: properties
inputs.about: Definitions for custom properties as a JSON string. Each must include a unique `property_name` (max 75 chars, no spaces) and `value_type`. Optional: `description`, `required`, `default_value`, `allowed_values` (for 'single_select' type).

tools.name: Create or update a custom property for an organization
tools.description: Creates a new custom property (name must be unique for creation) or updates an existing one for an organization to define metadata for its repositories.

inputs.name: org
inputs.about: The organization's unique identifier (case-insensitive).

inputs.name: required
inputs.about: If true, property must be set for all repositories and `default_value` is mandatory.

inputs.name: value_type
inputs.about: Data type of the custom property. Can be 'string' (free text), 'single_select' (single choice from list), 'multi_select' (multiple choices from list), 'true_false' (boolean), or 'url' (URL format).

inputs.name: description
inputs.about: Explanation of the custom property's purpose.

inputs.name: default_value
inputs.about: Default value if property isn't set. For `single_select` type, must be one of `allowed_values`. Can be a string for single values or an array for multi_select.

inputs.name: allowed_values
inputs.about: Ordered list of allowed values (up to 200). Required and non-empty if `value_type` is `single_select` or `multi_select`.

inputs.name: values_editable_by
inputs.about: Who can edit the values of the property. Can be 'org_actors' (organization actors only) or 'org_and_repo_actors' (organization and repository actors).

inputs.name: custom_property_name
inputs.about: Name of the custom property (case-sensitive).

tools.name: Create or update file contents
tools.description: Creates or updates a file in a GitHub repository with a commit message and supplied content. A missing non-default branch may result in the change being committed to the repository's default branch. Content may be supplied as plain text or Base64.

inputs.name: sha
inputs.about: The blob SHA of the file being replaced. Automatically fetched if not provided. If a 409 conflict occurs (SHA mismatch due to concurrent modifications), the action will automatically retry up to 5 times with exponential backoff and jitter.

inputs.name: path
inputs.about: The full path to the file in the repository, including the filename and extension. Do not include leading slashes.

inputs.name: repo
inputs.about: The name of the repository (not case sensitive, without the `.git` extension).

inputs.name: owner
inputs.about: The account owner of the repository (not case sensitive).

inputs.name: branch
inputs.about: The branch name. Defaults to the repository's default branch if omitted. If a non-existent branch is specified, the action will automatically fall back to the repository's default branch. For empty repositories, omitting this parameter is recommended to let GitHub initialize with the repository's co

inputs.name: content
inputs.about: The new file content. Can be provided as plain text (will be automatically encoded to Base64) or as Base64-encoded text. GitHub API requires Base64 encoding, which this action handles automatically.

inputs.name: message
inputs.about: The commit message for this file creation or update.

inputs.name: author__date
inputs.about: Author's timestamp (ISO 8601 format). Defaults to committer's date if author details are provided but date is not.

inputs.name: author__name
inputs.about: Author's name. If specified, `author_email` is also required. Defaults to committer details; if all committer/author details omitted, GitHub uses authenticated user.

inputs.name: author__email
inputs.about: Author's email. If specified, `author_name` is also required. Defaults to committer details; if all committer/author details omitted, GitHub uses authenticated user.

inputs.name: committer__date
inputs.about: Committer's commit timestamp (ISO 8601 format). Defaults to current time if committer details are provided but date is not.

inputs.name: committer__name
inputs.about: Committer's name. If specified, `committer_email` is also required. GitHub uses authenticated user if all committer/author details omitted.

inputs.name: committer__email
inputs.about: Committer's email. If specified, `committer_name` is also required. GitHub uses authenticated user if all committer/author details omitted.

tools.name: Create or Update GitHub Pages Site
tools.description: Enables or updates GitHub Pages configuration for a repository, including source, custom domain and HTTPS settings. The build type defaults to legacy, which requires a source branch even when updating an existing site.

inputs.name: repo
inputs.about: The name of the repository without the .git extension. Not case-sensitive.

inputs.name: cname
inputs.about: Custom domain for the Pages site (e.g., 'example.com'). Set to null to remove custom domain. Only used during updates.

inputs.name: owner
inputs.about: The account owner of the repository (username or organization). Not case-sensitive.

inputs.name: build_type
inputs.about: Build process type: 'legacy' for traditional GitHub Pages build from a branch, 'workflow' for GitHub Actions. When 'workflow', source_branch and source_path are ignored.

inputs.name: source_path
inputs.about: The directory path within source_branch containing the site files: '/' for root or '/docs' for docs folder. Ignored if build_type is 'workflow'.

inputs.name: source_branch
inputs.about: The repository branch to use for GitHub Pages source (e.g., 'main', 'gh-pages'). Required if build_type is 'legacy'. Ignored if build_type is 'workflow'.

inputs.name: https_enforced
inputs.about: Whether to enforce HTTPS for the Pages site. Only used during updates.

tools.name: Create or update repo secret with encrypted value

This action allows you to securely manage secrets for a given repository, ensuring that sensitive data remains protected during the update process. By providing the encrypted value alongside the key ID, you can seamlessly maintain the necessary credentials for your repository's operations.

inputs.name: repo
inputs.about: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This name is not case-sensitive.

inputs.name: owner
inputs.about: The account owner of the repository (e.g., a GitHub username or organization name). This name is not case-sensitive.

inputs.name: key_id
inputs.about: The ID of the public key that was used to encrypt the secret value. This ID is retrieved from GitHub along with the public key via the 'Get a repository public key' endpoint for Dependabot secrets. If not provided or if an outdated key_id is used, the action will automatically fetch the latest publi

inputs.name: secret_name
inputs.about: The name of the Dependabot secret to create or update.

inputs.name: encrypted_value
inputs.about: Value for your secret. This value must be encrypted with LibSodium, using the public key retrieved from the GitHub API's 'Get a repository public key' endpoint for Dependabot secrets. The resulting encrypted string is typically Base64 encoded.

tools.name: Create repository

inputs.name: private

inputs.name: has_wiki

inputs.name: homepage

inputs.name: has_downloads

inputs.name: has_discussions

inputs.name: allow_auto_merge

inputs.name: license_template

inputs.name: allow_merge_commit

inputs.name: allow_rebase_merge

inputs.name: allow_squash_merge
inputs.about: Whether to allow squash merges for pull requests. Default is true.

inputs.name: gitignore_template

inputs.name: merge_commit_title
inputs.about: Required when using merge_commit_message. The default value for a merge commit title: PR_TITLE (default to the pull request's title) or MERGE_MESSAGE (default to the classic title for a merge message).

inputs.name: merge_commit_message

inputs.name: delete_branch_on_merge
inputs.about: Whether to delete head branches when pull requests are merged. Default is false.

inputs.name: squash_merge_commit_title

inputs.name: squash_merge_commit_message
inputs.about: The default value for a squash merge commit message: PR_BODY (default to the pull request's body), COMMIT_MESSAGES (default to the branch's commit messages), or BLANK (default to a blank commit message).

tools.name: List workflow run artifacts

tools.name: List workflow runs for a repository
tools.description: Lists workflow runs for a repository, allowing filtering by actor, branch, event, status, creation date, check suite ID, or head SHA; the repository must exist and be accessible.

inputs.name: page
inputs.about: Page number of the results to fetch.

inputs.name: repo
inputs.about: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension (not case-sensitive).

inputs.name: actor
inputs.about: Filter by the actor's login (e.g., the user who triggered the `push`).

inputs.name: event
inputs.about: Filter by the event that triggered the workflow (e.g., `push`, `pull_request`).

inputs.name: owner
inputs.about: The account owner of the repository (not case-sensitive).

inputs.name: branch
inputs.about: Filter by branch name (e.g., `main` or the branch that triggered the `push`).

inputs.name: status
inputs.about: Filter by `status` or `conclusion` (e.g., `success`, `in_progress`). Note: Only GitHub Actions can set `waiting`, `pending`, or `requested`.

inputs.name: created
inputs.about: Filter by creation date or date-time range (ISO8601 format: YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ). Supports operators like `>`, `<`, `>=`, `<=`, and `..` for ranges.

inputs.name: head_sha
inputs.about: Filter to include only runs associated with the specified `head_sha` (commit SHA at the head of the branch).

inputs.name: per_page
inputs.about: Number of results per page (maximum 100).

inputs.name: check_suite_id
inputs.about: Filter by a specific `check_suite_id`.

inputs.name: exclude_pull_requests
inputs.about: Set to `true` to exclude workflow runs triggered by pull request events. Omit or leave as null to include all runs.

tools.name: List workflow runs for a workflow
tools.description: Lists runs for a specified, existing workflow (identified by ID or filename like `main.yml`) in a GitHub repository, with filtering options.

inputs.name: page
inputs.about: Page number of the results to retrieve.

inputs.name: repo
inputs.about: Repository name, without the `.git` extension (case-insensitive).

inputs.name: actor
inputs.about: Filter by the GitHub username of the actor who initiated the run.

inputs.name: event
inputs.about: Filter by the event that triggered the run (e.g., `push`, `pull_request`). For more event types, see GitHub's documentation on "Events that trigger workflows".

inputs.name: owner
inputs.about: Account owner of the repository (case-insensitive).

inputs.name: branch
inputs.about: Filter by branch name, typically for `push` events.

inputs.name: status
inputs.about: Filter by status or conclusion (e.g., `success`, `in_progress`). Note: `waiting`, `pending`, or `requested` statuses are set exclusively by GitHub Actions.

inputs.name: created
inputs.about: Filter by creation date/time range. For syntax, refer to GitHub's "Understanding the search syntax" guide for dates.

inputs.name: head_sha
inputs.about: Filter by the head commit's SHA.

inputs.name: per_page
inputs.about: Number of results per page (max 100).

inputs.name: workflow_id
inputs.about: The ID of the workflow (integer) or the workflow file name (string, e.g., `main.yml` or `ci.yaml`).

inputs.name: check_suite_id
inputs.about: Filter by `check_suite_id` (identifier for a collection of check runs).

inputs.name: exclude_pull_requests
inputs.about: If true, exclude workflow runs triggered by pull requests.

tools.name: Lock an issue
tools.description: Locks an existing GitHub issue's conversation, preventing further comments; an optional reason can be specified.

inputs.name: repo
inputs.about: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This name is not case-sensitive.

inputs.name: owner

inputs.name: lock_reason
inputs.about: Optional reason for locking the conversation. Valid values: 'off-topic', 'too heated', 'resolved', 'spam'. If omitted, no reason is displayed.

inputs.name: issue_number

tools.name: Lookup Enterprise Administrator Invitation

inputs.name: enterprise_slug
inputs.about: The slug of the enterprise the user was invited to join. This is the URL-friendly identifier for the enterprise.

tools.name: Lookup GitHub Resource
tools.description: Look up a GitHub resource by URL and return its GraphQL type and URL.

inputs.name: url
inputs.about: The GitHub URL of the resource to lookup. Can be a repository, issue, pull request, or other GitHub resource URL.

tools.name: Lookup nodes by IDs
tools.description: Look up multiple GitHub nodes by their global node IDs in a single GraphQL query, returning each node's ID and type.

inputs.name: ids
inputs.about: A list of GitHub global node IDs to lookup. Each ID must be a valid base64-encoded global node ID (e.g., 'MDQ6VXNlcjU4MzIzMQ==').

tools.name: Lookup Organization (GraphQL)
tools.description: Tool to lookup a GitHub organization by login using GraphQL. Use when you need organization information via GraphQL API.

inputs.name: login

tools.name: Look Up Topic by Name
tools.description: Tool to look up a GitHub topic by name using GraphQL. Use when you need to find information about a specific GitHub topic including its popularity (stargazer count) and related topics.

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: The topic's name to look up (e.g., 'python', 'javascript', 'machine-learning').

inputs.name: related_topics_count
inputs.about: The number of related topics to fetch (between 1 and 10). Only used if include_related_topics is true.

inputs.name: include_related_topics
inputs.about: Whether to include related topics in the response. If true, up to 3 related topics will be returned.

tools.name: Manage access control for organization codespaces
tools.description: Sets the Codespaces access control policy for a GitHub organization, determining which members can use them. This endpoint requires admin permissions on the organization. The API returns HTTP 204 No Content on success.

inputs.name: org
inputs.about: The name of the GitHub organization (case-insensitive). The authenticated user must have admin permissions on this organization.

inputs.name: visibility
inputs.about:
Defines which users can access Codespaces within the organization.
`disabled`: Codespaces are disabled for all users in the organization.
`selected_members`: Only users specified in `selected_usernames` can access Codespaces.
`all_members`: All members of the organization can access Codespaces.
`all

inputs.name: selected_usernames
inputs.about: A list of GitHub usernames who should have access to Codespaces. Required when `visibility` is set to `selected_members`. Providing a list here will replace any existing list of selected usernames. The specified users must be members or outside collaborators of the organization.

tools.name: Manage custom properties for org repos
tools.description: Creates or updates values for an organization's predefined custom properties across multiple repositories (up to 30).

inputs.name: org
inputs.about: The organization's name (case-insensitive).

inputs.name: repository_names
inputs.about: Repository names (max 30) to apply the custom property values to.

tools.name: Manage issue blocking dependency

inputs.name: secret_name

inputs.name: email

inputs.name: owner

inputs.name: author_id

tools.name: Mark a thread as done

inputs.name: thread_id
inputs.about: ID of the notification thread to mark as done. Typically obtained from the `id` field in notification list operations (e.g., `GET /notifications`).

tools.name: Mark a thread as read
tools.description: Marks an existing GitHub notification thread, identified by its `thread_id`, as read.

inputs.name: thread_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the notification thread. This ID is obtained from a notification's `id` field, for example, via the 'List notifications for the authenticated user' endpoint.

tools.name: Mark notifications as read
tools.description: Marks notifications as read or unread, optionally for those updated at or before a `last_read_at` timestamp.

inputs.name: read
inputs.about: Indicates whether to mark targeted notifications as read (`true`) or unread (`false`). Defaults to `true` (mark as read) if not provided.

inputs.name: last_read_at
inputs.about: If provided, only notifications updated at or before this timestamp are affected. If omitted, all current notifications are targeted.

tools.name: Mark pull request ready for review
tools.description: Marks a draft pull request as ready for review using GitHub GraphQL API, transitioning it from draft to reviewable state. Use this action when a draft pull request has reached a stage where it is ready for team review and can potentially be merged. This action cannot be used on pull requests that are already marked as ready for review.

inputs.name: pull_request_id
inputs.about: The global Node ID of the pull request to mark as ready for review (e.g., 'PR_kwDOABCDEFGHIJK'). This is the GraphQL ID, not the numeric pull request number. You can obtain this ID from the 'node_id' field when listing or getting pull requests.

inputs.name: client_mutation_id
inputs.about: A unique identifier for the client performing the mutation. Used to ensure idempotency of mutations and track the request.

tools.name: Mark repository notifications as read
tools.description: Marks notifications in a repository as read; if 'last_read_at' is specified, notifications updated after this timestamp are not marked as read.

inputs.name: repo
inputs.about: Name of the repository, without the `.git` extension (case-insensitive).

inputs.name: owner
inputs.about: Username of the account owning the repository (case-insensitive).

inputs.name: last_read_at
inputs.about: Timestamp (ISO 8601 format: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`). If provided, notifications updated *after* this time will NOT be marked as read. If omitted, all notifications in the repository are marked as read. Defaults to the current time.

tools.name: Merge a branch

inputs.name: base
inputs.about: The name of the branch to merge the `head` branch into.

inputs.name: head
inputs.about: Source branch name or full commit SHA to merge into the `base` branch.

inputs.name: repo
inputs.about: Repository name, without the `.git` extension. Not case-sensitive.

inputs.name: owner
inputs.about: Username or organization name of the repository owner. Not case-sensitive.

inputs.name: commit_message
inputs.about: Commit message for the merge. If omitted, GitHub uses a default message.

tools.name: Merge a pull request
tools.description: Merges an open and mergeable pull request in a repository. A 405 error can occur for multiple reasons: (1) The PR is still in draft mode - convert it to ready-for-review first using GITHUB_UPDATE_A_PULL_REQUEST. (2) Branch protection rules are not satisfied - check for required approving reviews, status checks, or other repository rules that must be met before merging. (3) The base branch has been modified since the PR was last synced - update the PR branch first using GITHUB_UPDATE_A_PULL_REQUEST_BRANCH.

inputs.name: sha
inputs.about: SHA of the pull request's head commit. Must match for merge to succeed, ensuring PR hasn't changed since review.

inputs.name: repo
inputs.about: Repository name, without the `.git` extension. Not case-sensitive.

inputs.name: owner
inputs.about: Repository owner's username. Not case-sensitive.

inputs.name: pull_number
inputs.about: The unique number identifying the pull request. The PR must be mergeable: not a draft, and all branch protection rules (required reviews, status checks, etc.) must be satisfied.

inputs.name: commit_title
inputs.about: Title for the merge commit message.

inputs.name: merge_method
inputs.about: Merge strategy: 'merge', 'squash', or 'rebase'. Defaults to repository's setting if unspecified.

inputs.name: commit_message
inputs.about: Additional details for the merge commit message.

tools.name: Move a project card (Classic - Deprecated)
tools.description: Moves a project card to a specified position within a column (GitHub Classic Projects). DEPRECATION NOTICE: GitHub Projects (classic) and its REST API were sunset on April 1, 2025. This action will return 404 for most requests on GitHub.com. It may still work on GitHub Enterprise Server instances where classic projects remain enabled. For new projects, use GitHub Projects V2 which uses the GraphQL API instead. See: https://github.blog/changelog/2024-05-23-sunset-notice-projects-classic/ On success, the API returns HTTP 201 with an empty body, indicating the card was moved.

inputs.name: card_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the project card to be moved. Obtain this ID from the list_project_cards or get_a_project_card actions.

inputs.name: position
inputs.about: The target position of the card within the column. Must be one of: 'top' (place card at top of column), 'bottom' (place card at bottom of column), or 'after:<card_id>' (place card immediately after the specified card). When using 'after:<card_id>', the referenced card must exist in the target column

inputs.name: column_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the column to move the card to. If omitted, the card stays in its current column but moves to the specified position.

tools.name: Move a project column (Classic - Deprecated)
tools.description: Moves a column within a GitHub Classic Project to the first or last position, or after a specified column. DEPRECATED: The Classic Projects REST API has been sunset and this action no longer works on GitHub.com. Use GitHub Projects V2 with the GraphQL API for new projects.

inputs.name: position
inputs.about: The new position for the column within the project. Valid values are: 'first' (move to the beginning), 'last' (move to the end), or 'after:<column_id>' (place after the specified column, e.g., 'after:67890').

inputs.name: column_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the project column to be moved. Must be a valid column ID from a GitHub project (classic).

tools.name: Ping an organization webhook

inputs.name: hook_id

tools.name: Ping a repository webhook

inputs.name: owner
inputs.about: The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.

inputs.name: hook_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the hook. You can find this value in the `X-GitHub-Hook-ID` header of a webhook delivery.

tools.name: Privately report a security vulnerability
tools.description: Privately reports a security vulnerability to a repository's maintainers. IMPORTANT: You cannot report vulnerabilities to repositories you own - this API is for third-party security researchers to report to other repositories. The target repository must have private vulnerability reporting enabled. Specify EITHER `severity` OR `cvss_vector_string`, but not both.

inputs.name: repo
inputs.about: The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. This name is not case-sensitive.

inputs.name: owner
inputs.about: The account owner of the repository. This name is not case-sensitive.

inputs.name: cwe_ids
inputs.about: A list of Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) identifiers relevant to the vulnerability.

inputs.name: summary
inputs.about: A short, descriptive summary of the security vulnerability.

inputs.name: severity
inputs.about: The advisory's severity level. Mutually exclusive with `cvss_vector_string`.

inputs.name: description
inputs.about: A detailed explanation of the security vulnerability, its impact, and potential mitigations.

inputs.name: vulnerabilities
inputs.about: JSON string representing a list of vulnerability objects detailing the affected packages or products. Each object should specify the package's ecosystem and name, the vulnerable version range, and optionally, patched versions and vulnerable functions.

inputs.name: cvss_vector_string
inputs.about: The CVSS vector string for advisory severity. Mutually exclusive with `severity`.

inputs.name: start_private_fork
inputs.about: Whether to create a temporary private fork to collaborate on a fix for the reported vulnerability.

tools.name: Publish Sponsors Tier (GraphQL)

inputs.name: username

inputs.name: username

inputs.name: team_slug

inputs.name: org
