inputs.name: role_id

inputs.name: username

tools.name: Remove app access restrictions

inputs.name: repo

inputs.name: owner

inputs.name: branch
inputs.about: The name of the branch from which all app access restrictions will be removed. Wildcard characters are not supported; for branches with wildcards, please use the GraphQL API.

tools.name: Remove a project from a team
tools.description: Removes a classic project from a team within an organization.

inputs.name: org
inputs.about: The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.

inputs.name: team_slug

inputs.name: project_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the project to be removed from the team.

tools.name: Remove a repository collaborator

inputs.name: owner

inputs.name: username
inputs.about: The GitHub username of the collaborator to remove.

tools.name: Remove a repository from an app installation

inputs.about: The unique identifier of the repository to be removed from the installation.

inputs.name: installation_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the GitHub App installation from which to remove the repository.

tools.name: Remove a repository from a team
tools.description: Disassociates a repository from a team; team members may lose access permissions, but the repository and team are not deleted.

inputs.name: org
inputs.about: The name of the organization where the team and repository exist. This field is case-insensitive.

inputs.name: repo
inputs.about: The name of the repository, without the '.git' extension. This field is case-insensitive.

inputs.name: owner
inputs.about: The username of the account that owns the repository. This field is case-insensitive.

inputs.name: team_slug
inputs.about: The URL-friendly identifier (slug) for the team. Team slugs are typically all lowercase with hyphens instead of spaces (e.g., 'justice-league' for 'Justice League').

tools.name: Remove a selected repository from a user secret
tools.description: Removes a selected repository's access to a user's Codespaces secret; the secret must exist and the repository must have previously been granted access.

inputs.name: secret_name
inputs.about: Name of the user's Codespaces secret from which repository access will be revoked.

inputs.name: repository_id
inputs.about: The unique integer identifier of the repository that will lose access to the specified Codespaces secret.

tools.name: Remove assignees from an issue
tools.description: Removes specified assignees from a GitHub issue; requires push access, and invalid removal attempts are silently ignored.

inputs.name: repo
inputs.about: The name of the repository, excluding the `.git` extension. This name is not case-sensitive.

inputs.name: owner

inputs.name: assignees
inputs.about: Usernames to unassign from the issue. Note: Requires push access to the repository; attempts to remove users without permission or those not currently assigned are silently ignored.

inputs.name: issue_number
inputs.about: The unique number that identifies the issue within the repository.

tools.name: Remove custom label from repo runner
tools.description: Removes a custom label from a repository's self-hosted runner; this operation is idempotent.

inputs.about: Name of the custom label to remove from the self-hosted runner. Note: only custom labels can be removed; read-only system labels (like 'self-hosted', 'linux', 'x64') cannot be removed.

inputs.name: repo
inputs.about: Repository name, without the `.git` extension (case-insensitive).

inputs.name: owner
inputs.about: Account owner of the repository (case-insensitive).

inputs.name: runner_id
inputs.about: Unique identifier of the self-hosted runner. Get this from listing runners for the repository.

tools.name: Remove custom label from self hosted runner
tools.description: Removes a currently assigned custom label (`name`) from a self-hosted runner (`runner_id`) in an organization (`org`). This action allows the organization to manage the labels associated with their runners effectively.

inputs.name: org
inputs.about: The name of the organization. This name is not case-sensitive.

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: The name of the custom label to remove from the self-hosted runner.

inputs.name: runner_id
inputs.about: Unique identifier of the self-hosted runner.

tools.name: Remove custom labels from self hosted repo runner
tools.description: Removes all custom labels from a self-hosted runner registered at the repository level, leaving only its default labels and any labels inherited from its runner group or organization.

inputs.name: repo
inputs.about: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This name is not case-sensitive.

inputs.name: owner
inputs.about: The account owner of the repository. This name is not case-sensitive.

inputs.name: runner_id
inputs.about: Unique identifier (ID) of the self-hosted runner.

tools.name: Remove interaction restrictions for an organization
tools.description: Removes all interaction restrictions from public repositories in the specified GitHub organization, allowing all users to resume interactions.

inputs.name: org
inputs.about: The name of the GitHub organization. This name is not case-sensitive.

tools.name: Remove interaction restrictions for a repository
tools.description: Removes all interaction restrictions for a repository, enabling all users to comment, open issues, and create pull requests by lifting any existing temporary interaction limits.

inputs.name: repo
inputs.about: Repository name, without the `.git` extension; case-insensitive.

inputs.name: owner
inputs.about: Username or organization name of the repository owner; case-insensitive.

tools.name: Remove org dev env secret by name
tools.description: Deletes a named GitHub Codespaces secret from an organization. A not-found response is treated as success, so success does not necessarily confirm that a secret was deleted.

inputs.name: org
inputs.about: Name of the GitHub organization (case-insensitive).

inputs.name: secret_name
inputs.about: Name of the Codespaces secret to remove.

tools.name: Remove org secret by name
tools.description: Permanently removes a specific Dependabot secret, by its `secret_name`, from the GitHub `org`, making it unavailable to Dependabot for that organization.

inputs.name: org
inputs.about: GitHub organization name (case-insensitive).

inputs.name: secret_name
inputs.about: Dependabot secret name to remove from the organization.

tools.name: Remove outside collaborator from an organization
tools.description: Removes a user, who must be an outside collaborator, from the specified GitHub organization, revoking their access to all its repositories.

inputs.name: org
inputs.about: The name of the GitHub organization. This name is not case-sensitive.

inputs.name: username
inputs.about: The GitHub username of the outside collaborator to remove.

tools.name: Remove public org membership
tools.description: Removes the authenticated user's public organization membership, making it private. The user remains a member of the organization but their membership is no longer publicly visible. This operation is idempotent - calling it when the membership is already private will succeed.

inputs.name: org
inputs.about: Name of the GitHub organization (case-insensitive). The authenticated user must be a member of this organization.

inputs.name: username
inputs.about: GitHub username of the authenticated user. Must match the currently authenticated user - you can only modify your own public membership status.

tools.name: Remove user public repo interaction restrictions
tools.description: Removes all interaction restrictions (limitations on comments, issues, or pull requests) from all public repositories owned by the authenticated user.

tools.name: Remove repository from organization dev environment secret
tools.description: Removes a repository's access to an organization-level Codespaces secret, if it was previously granted.

inputs.name: org
inputs.about: The GitHub organization name (not case-sensitive).

inputs.name: secret_name
inputs.about: The Codespaces secret name.

inputs.name: repository_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the repository.

tools.name: Remove selected repo from org secret
tools.description: Revokes a specific repository's access to an organization-level Dependabot secret, applicable only when the secret has 'selected' visibility and the specified repository currently has access.

inputs.name: org
inputs.about: Name of the organization (not case-sensitive).

inputs.name: secret_name
inputs.about: Name of the Dependabot secret.

inputs.name: repository_id
inputs.about: Unique numeric ID of the repository (not the repository name).

tools.name: Remove requested reviewers from a pull request
tools.description: Removes currently assigned user logins and/or team slugs from a GitHub pull request's list of requested reviewers.

inputs.name: repo
inputs.about: Repository name, without the `.git` extension (not case-sensitive).

inputs.name: owner
inputs.about: Username of the repository owner (not case-sensitive).

inputs.name: reviewers
inputs.about: GitHub user `login`s for removal. At least one of `reviewers` or `team_reviewers` must be specified.

inputs.name: pull_number
inputs.about: Number of the pull request.

inputs.name: team_reviewers
inputs.about: GitHub team `slug`s (URL-friendly names) for removal. At least one of `reviewers` or `team_reviewers` must be specified.

tools.name: Remove review request
tools.description: Removes requested reviewers from a pull request. Use this action when you need to cancel a review request that was previously sent to users or teams. Only users with push access to the repository can remove review requests.

inputs.name: repo
inputs.about: The name of the repository without the .git extension. The name is not case sensitive.

inputs.name: owner
inputs.about: The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.

inputs.name: reviewers
inputs.about: An array of user logins that will be removed from the review request.

inputs.name: pull_number
inputs.about: The number that identifies the pull request.

inputs.name: team_reviewers
inputs.about: An array of team slugs that will be removed from the review request.

tools.name: Remove selected repository from an organization secret
tools.description: Removes a specific repository's access to an organization-level secret; the repository must have been previously granted access to this secret.

inputs.name: org
inputs.about: Organization name (case-insensitive).

inputs.name: secret_name
inputs.about: Name of the organization secret.

inputs.name: repository_id
inputs.about: Repository ID to remove from the secret's access.

tools.name: Remove selected repository from an organization variable
tools.description: Removes a repository's access to an organization variable that has 'selected' visibility. This endpoint removes a specific repository from an organization variable's access list. The variable must have its visibility set to 'selected' for this operation to work. Returns a 409 Conflict error if the variable visibility is not 'selected'.

inputs.name: org
inputs.about: The organization's name (case-insensitive).

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: Name of the organization variable.

inputs.name: repository_id
inputs.about: Unique identifier of the repository.

tools.name: Remove status check contexts
tools.description: Removes specified status check contexts from a protected branch's required status checks. This action removes the specified status check contexts from the existing list of required status checks for a protected branch. The branch must already have branch protection enabled with status checks configured. Note: The 'contexts' parameter is deprecated by GitHub in favor of 'checks' array. For new implementations, consider using update_status_check_protection with the 'checks' parameter instead.

inputs.name: repo
inputs.about: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This name is not case sensitive.

inputs.name: owner
inputs.about: The account owner of the repository. This name is not case sensitive.

inputs.name: branch
inputs.about: The name of the branch. Wildcard characters are not allowed. To use wildcard characters in branch names, refer to the GraphQL API documentation.

inputs.name: contexts
inputs.about: The status check contexts to remove from the protected branch. These are the names of CI/CD jobs or other checks that should no longer be required before merging. Can be provided as a single string or a list of strings. Examples: 'ci/test', 'linter', 'continuous-integration/travis-ci'.

tools.name: Remove status check protection
tools.description: Removes status check protection from a branch, disabling required status checks for merging pull requests; will only have an effect if status check protection is currently configured on the branch.

inputs.name: repo
inputs.about: Name of the repository, without the `.git` extension; not case-sensitive.

inputs.name: owner
inputs.about: Account owner (username or organization) of the repository; not case-sensitive.

inputs.name: branch
inputs.about: Name of the branch; wildcard characters are not allowed.

tools.name: Remove team access restrictions
tools.description: Removes specified teams from push access to a protected branch. This action removes teams from the list of teams with push access to a protected branch. Removing a team will also remove push access for any child teams. Prerequisites: - The repository must be owned by an organization (not a personal account) - The branch must have protection rules enabled - The branch protection must have restrictions configured - The teams must currently have push access to the branch

inputs.name: repo
inputs.about: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This value is not case-sensitive.

inputs.name: owner
inputs.about: The organization name that owns the repository. Team access restrictions only work for organization-owned repositories, not personal repositories. This value is not case-sensitive.

inputs.name: teams
inputs.about: The list of team slugs to remove from push access to the protected branch. A team slug is the URL-friendly version of the team name (lowercase, hyphens instead of spaces). Removing a team will also remove push access for any child teams. This removes teams from the existing list (does not replace th

inputs.name: branch
inputs.about: The name of the protected branch to remove team restrictions from. The branch must already have branch protection enabled with restrictions configured. Wildcard characters are not supported. For wildcard branch protection, use the GitHub GraphQL API.

tools.name: Remove team membership
tools.description: Tool to remove team membership for a user in an organization. Use when you need to revoke a user's membership from a specific team. This action is irreversible — the user must be explicitly re-added if you want to restore their team membership. Note that if team synchronization is set up, this operation may fail with a 403 Forbidden error.

inputs.name: org
inputs.about: The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.

inputs.name: username
inputs.about: The handle for the GitHub user account.

inputs.name: team_slug
inputs.about: The slug of the team name.

tools.name: Remove team membership for a user
tools.description: Removes a user from a specific team within an organization. This action requires admin:org scope permissions. It will fail if: - Team synchronization with an Identity Provider (IdP) is enabled (403 Forbidden) - The organization, team, or user membership doesn't exist (404 Not Found) - You don't have sufficient permissions to manage team memberships (403 Forbidden) Note: If the removed user was the last member and the team is not nested, the team may be deleted automatically.

inputs.name: org
inputs.about: The name of the GitHub organization that owns the team. Not case-sensitive.

inputs.name: username
inputs.about: The GitHub username of the user to remove from the team. Must be an exact match of the user's login handle.

inputs.name: team_slug
inputs.about: The URL-friendly identifier (slug) of the team. This is the hyphenated, lowercase version of the team name as it appears in the team's URL (e.g., 'justice-league' for a team named 'Justice League').

tools.name: Remove user access restrictions
tools.description: Removes specified users from the list of people allowed to push to a protected branch. Important notes: - This action only works on organization-owned repositories (not personal repos) - The branch must have protection rules with push restrictions enabled - Users being removed must currently have push access to the branch - The combined total of users, apps, and teams is limited to 100 items

inputs.name: repo
inputs.about: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. Not case-sensitive.

inputs.name: owner
inputs.about: The account owner of the repository. Must be an organization name (user access restrictions only work on organization repositories). Not case-sensitive.

inputs.name: users
inputs.about: The list of user logins to remove from push access to the protected branch. These users will no longer be able to push directly to this branch. The combined total of users, apps, and teams with restrictions is limited to 100 items.

inputs.name: branch
inputs.about: The name of the branch from which to remove user access restrictions. Wildcard characters (e.g., '*') are not allowed. Use the GitHub GraphQL API for wildcard branch patterns.

tools.name: Remove user as a collaborator (classic project)
tools.description: Removes a user as a collaborator from an organization project (classic); a success result can also indicate that the user was already absent. The Projects (classic) REST API is sunset on GitHub.com and may still work on GitHub Enterprise Server versions before 3.17.

inputs.name: username
inputs.about: The GitHub username of the user to remove as a collaborator from the organization project (classic).

inputs.name: project_id
inputs.about: The unique database identifier of the organization project (classic). This is a numeric ID returned when listing or creating classic projects, not the project number visible in URLs.

tools.name: Remove users from codespaces access for an organization
tools.description: Removes selected users from GitHub Codespaces billing access for an existing organization.

inputs.name: org
inputs.about: The name of the GitHub organization. This field is not case-sensitive.

inputs.name: selected_usernames
inputs.about: A list of GitHub usernames, typically organization members. After removal, the organization will no longer be billed for Codespaces created by these users.

tools.name: Rename a branch
tools.description: Renames an existing branch in a GitHub repository; the new name must be unique and adhere to GitHub's naming conventions, and the current branch name cannot contain wildcard characters.

inputs.name: repo
inputs.about: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.

inputs.name: owner
inputs.about: The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.

inputs.name: branch
inputs.about: The current name of the branch. Wildcard characters (e.g., `*`) are not allowed.

inputs.name: new_name
inputs.about: The new name for the branch. Must be unique and adhere to GitHub's branch naming conventions (e.g., no spaces, '..', or leading/trailing slashes).

tools.name: Render a markdown document
tools.description: Renders Markdown to HTML; for 'gfm' mode, provide 'context' (owner/repo) to correctly link issues, pull requests, and user mentions.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.about: Rendering mode: 'markdown' for standard Markdown or 'gfm' for GitHub Flavored Markdown.

inputs.name: text
inputs.about: The Markdown string to convert to HTML.

inputs.name: context
inputs.about: The repository context (e.g., 'owner/repo') used when `mode` is 'gfm'.

tools.name: Render Markdown (Raw Mode)
tools.description: Tool to render raw Markdown text to HTML using GitHub's markdown API. Use when you need to convert plain Markdown content to HTML without GitHub-specific features like issue references or @mentions.

inputs.name: markdown_content
inputs.about: The raw Markdown text to render as HTML. This can include any valid Markdown syntax like headers, lists, links, bold/italic text, code blocks, etc.

tools.name: Reopen an issue
tools.description: Reopens a closed GitHub issue by changing its state to 'open' with state_reason 'reopened'. Use this action when you need to reopen a previously closed issue that requires further attention or work. Only users with push access to the repository can reopen issues.

inputs.name: repo
inputs.about: The name of the repository without the .git extension (case-insensitive).

inputs.name: owner
inputs.about: The account owner of the repository (case-insensitive).

inputs.name: issue_number
inputs.about: The number that identifies the issue.

tools.name: Reopen Pull Request
tools.description: Reopens a previously closed pull request by setting its state to 'open'. This restores the pull request to an active state where it can be reviewed, commented on, and merged. Use this action when you need to reactivate a closed pull request that was closed prematurely or needs to be reconsidered for merging.

inputs.name: repo
inputs.about: The name of the repository without the .git extension. The name is not case sensitive.

inputs.name: owner
inputs.about: The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.

inputs.name: pull_number
inputs.about: The number that identifies the pull request.

tools.name: Replace all repository topics
tools.description: Replaces all topics of a repository.

inputs.name: repo
inputs.about: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This is case-insensitive.

inputs.name: names
inputs.about: A list of topic names to replace the current set of topics for the repository. Provide one or more topics to set them. To remove all topics, pass an empty list (`[]`). Note: Topic names cannot contain uppercase letters and are limited to 25 characters.

inputs.name: owner
inputs.about: The username of the account that owns the repository. This is case-insensitive.

tools.name: Replace org secret visibility to selected
tools.description: Replaces the list of repositories that can access a Dependabot organization secret when the secret's visibility is already set to 'selected'.

inputs.name: org
inputs.about: The name of the organization. This parameter is not case-sensitive.

inputs.name: secret_name
inputs.about: Name of the Dependabot secret (alphanumeric characters and underscores only, no spaces allowed).

inputs.name: selected_repository_ids
inputs.about: Array of repository IDs that can access this organization Dependabot secret. This list completely replaces any current repository associations. For incremental changes (add/remove individual repos), use dedicated add/remove repository secret actions instead.

tools.name: Replace repository access for an org Codespaces secret
tools.description: Replaces the list of repositories that can access an organization-level Codespaces secret. This operation completely replaces the existing list of repositories with the provided list. The secret must already have its visibility set to 'selected' for this operation to succeed. Use this when you want to set an exact list of repositories that should have access. Prerequisites: - The organization must exist and you must have admin:org scope - The Codespaces secret must already exist in the organization - The secret's visibility must be set to 'selected' (not 'all' or 'private') Returns HTTP 204 No Content on success, 404 if secret/org not found, 409 if visibility is not 'selected'.

inputs.name: org
inputs.about: The GitHub organization name (case-insensitive).

inputs.name: secret_name
inputs.about: Name of the development environment secret for which repository access is being configured.

inputs.name: selected_repository_ids
inputs.about: Array of repository IDs that can access the organization Codespaces secret. This completely replaces any existing list of repositories. Note: The secret's visibility must already be set to 'selected' (not 'all' or 'private') for this operation to succeed; otherwise, a 409 Conflict error is returned.

tools.name: Request a github pages build
tools.description: Manually triggers a GitHub Pages build for a repository if GitHub Pages is enabled, useful for deployments not automatically built or for retrying failed builds.

inputs.name: repo
inputs.about: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This name is not case-sensitive.

inputs.name: owner
inputs.about: The account owner of the repository. This name is not case-sensitive.

tools.name: Request reviewers for a pull request
tools.description: Requests reviewers for a specific pull request identified by owner, repository, and pull request number. inputs.name: repo
inputs.about: Name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. Not case sensitive.

inputs.name: owner
inputs.about: Account owner of the repository (username or organization name). Not case sensitive.

inputs.name: reviewers

inputs.name: team_reviewers

tools.name: Add reviewers to a specific pull request
tools.description: Adds reviewers to a specific pull request identified by owner, repo, and pull_number. This is NOT a search action - it operates on an already-known PR number. Requires `owner`, `repo`, `pull_number`, and at least one of `reviewers` or `team_reviewers`.

inputs.name: repo
inputs.about: Name of the repository, without the `.git` extension; not case sensitive.

inputs.name: owner
inputs.about: Account owner of the repository (username or organization name); not case sensitive.

inputs.name: reviewers
inputs.about: GitHub user `login` strings (usernames) to request reviews from. At least one of `reviewers` or `team_reviewers` must be provided.

inputs.name: pull_number
inputs.about: Number identifying the pull request.

inputs.name: team_reviewers
inputs.about: GitHub team `slug` strings (e.g., 'justice-league') to request reviews from. Slugs are typically lowercase and use hyphens for spaces. At least one of `reviewers` or `team_reviewers` must be provided.

tools.name: Rerequest a check run
tools.description: Triggers a re-run of a specific check run in a GitHub repository, resetting its status to 'queued', clearing its conclusion, and triggering the `check_run` webhook with `rerequested` action. IMPORTANT: This endpoint requires GitHub App authentication with 'checks:write' permission. The check run can ONLY be re-requested by the same GitHub App that originally created it. OAuth tokens and personal access tokens (PAT) cannot use this endpoint.

inputs.name: repo
inputs.about: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This field is case-insensitive.

inputs.name: owner
inputs.about: The account owner of the repository (username or organization name). This field is case-insensitive.

inputs.name: check_run_id
inputs.about: The unique numerical identifier of the check run to be re-requested. Must be a check run created by the same GitHub App making the request.

tools.name: Rerequest a check suite
tools.description: Triggers a new run of an existing check suite within a repository, resetting its status to 'queued', clearing its conclusion, and triggering the `check_suite` webhook with `rerequested` action. IMPORTANT: This endpoint requires GitHub App authentication with 'checks:write' permission. OAuth tokens and classic personal access tokens (PAT) cannot use this endpoint. Only GitHub App user access tokens, GitHub App installation access tokens, or fine-grained personal access tokens with checks:write permission are supported.

inputs.name: repo
inputs.about: The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. This field is case-insensitive.

inputs.name: owner
inputs.about: The account owner of the repository (username or organization name). This field is case-insensitive.

inputs.name: check_suite_id
inputs.about: The unique numerical identifier of the check suite to be re-requested. You can obtain this from the list_check_suites_for_a_git_reference endpoint or from a workflow run.

tools.name: Re-run a job from a workflow run
tools.description: Re-runs a specific job and any dependent jobs from a GitHub Actions workflow run in the specified repository, optionally enabling debug logging.

inputs.name: repo
inputs.about: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This name is not case sensitive.

inputs.name: owner
inputs.about: The account owner of the repository (e.g., a GitHub username or organization name). This name is not case sensitive.

inputs.name: job_id
inputs.about: The unique numerical identifier of the job to be re-run. This ID can be obtained by listing jobs for a workflow run.

tools.name: Run GraphQL Query

Cost-based rate limit: ~5,000 points/hour; keep field selections narrow, avoid deep nesting, and include rateLimit in responses to monitor quota. Responses are nested under data.data (e.g., data.data.repository.vulnerabilityAlerts); always inspect the errors array even on HTTP 200, as partial failures embed there. Paginate by looping on pageInfo.hasNextPage and advancing with pageInfo.endCursor. Search results cap at ~1,000 items per query; split by label, date range, or repository for full coverage. Use ProjectV2 nodes, not Classic Projects (deprecated). Parallel mutations (e.g., addProjectV2ItemById) can trigger transient conflicts; use sequential execution.

tools.name: Set interaction restrictions for an organization

tools.name: Set interaction restrictions for a repository

inputs.name: expiry

inputs.name: expiry

tools.name: Set allowed actions and workflows for an organization

tools.name: Set custom labels for repo runner

inputs.name: selected_repository_ids

tools.name: Set selected repositories for an organization secret

inputs.name: org

inputs.name: secret_name

inputs.name: selected_repository_ids

tools.name: Set selected repositories for a user secret

inputs.name: selected_repository_ids

tools.name: Set status check contexts

inputs.name: repo

inputs.name: owner

inputs.name: branch

tools.name: Set team access restrictions
tools.description: Replaces the list of teams with push access to a protected branch. This action sets (replaces) the teams that have push access to a protected branch. Unlike 'Add team access restrictions' (POST), this action replaces the entire list rather than adding to it. Use an empty list to remove all team restrictions. Prerequisites: - The repository must be owned by an organization (not a personal account) - The branch must have protection rules enabled - The branch protection must have restrictions configured - The teams must exist in the organization and have repository access

inputs.name: repo
inputs.about: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This value is not case-sensitive.

inputs.name: owner
inputs.about: The organization name that owns the repository. Team access restrictions only work for organization-owned repositories, not personal repositories. This value is not case-sensitive.

inputs.name: teams
inputs.about: The list of team slugs to grant push access to the protected branch. A team slug is the URL-friendly version of the team name (lowercase, hyphens instead of spaces). The teams must already have access to the repository. This REPLACES the entire existing list of teams with push access (use empty list

inputs.name: branch
inputs.about: The name of the protected branch to set team restrictions on. The branch must already have branch protection enabled with restrictions configured. Wildcard characters are not supported. For wildcard branch protection, use the GitHub GraphQL API.

tools.name: Set user access restrictions
tools.description: Replaces the list of users with push access to a protected branch in an organization repository. Important notes: - This action only works on organization-owned repositories (not personal repos) - The branch must already have protection rules with restrictions enabled - This REPLACES (not adds to) the existing list of users with push access - Users must have write access to the repository to be added - The combined total of users, apps, and teams is limited to 100 items - To add users without replacing, use the 'add_user_access_restrictions' action instead

inputs.name: repo
inputs.about: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This name is not case-sensitive.

inputs.name: owner
inputs.about: The account owner of the repository (must be an organization for user restrictions). This name is not case-sensitive.

inputs.name: users
inputs.about: The list of user logins (usernames) to grant push access to the protected branch. This REPLACES the existing list of users. Users must have write access to the repository. Pass an empty list [] to remove all user restrictions. The combined total of users, apps, and teams is limited to 100 items.

inputs.name: branch
inputs.about: The name of the branch. Cannot contain wildcard characters. To use wildcards in branch names, use the GitHub GraphQL API.

inputs.name: clientMutationId

tools.name: Set workflow access level outside repository

Specifies the level of access workflows outside this repository have to its actions and reusable workflows.

- `user`: Actions and reusable workflows can be shared with other private repositories owned

tools.name: Start a codespace for the authenticated user

tools.name: Stop a codespace for an organization user
tools.description: Stops a running codespace for an organization member. This action allows organization administrators to stop a codespace that belongs to a member of their organization. The codespace must be in a running state (e.g., 'Available') to be stopped. Required permissions: - OAuth/PAT: admin:org scope - Fine-grained tokens: 'Organization codespaces' (write) or 'Codespaces lifecycle admin' (write) Common HTTP responses: - 200: Codespace successfully stopped, returns codespace object - 304: Not modified (codespace already stopped) - 401: Authentication required - 403: Insufficient permissions (need admin:org) - 404: Organization, user, or codespace not found

inputs.name: codespace_name
inputs.about: The unique name of the codespace to stop. This is typically a hyphenated string like 'username-repo-name-randomchars'. You can obtain this from the 'List codespaces for a user in organization' action.

tools.name: Stop a codespace for the authenticated user

inputs.name: codespace_name

tools.name: Submit a review for a pull request

tools.name: Unlock an organization repository
tools.description: Unlocks a repository that was locked for migration within a GitHub organization. This action is part of the organization migrations workflow. When you start a migration with `lock_repositories=true`, the source repositories are locked to prevent changes during export. After the migration is complete and applied to the target instance, use this action to unlock the repositories so they can be accessed or deleted. Requirements: - You must be an organization owner to unlock repositories - The repository must be currently locked as part of the specified migration - This endpoint does not work with GitHub App tokens or fine-grained personal access tokens Typical workflow: 1. Start an organization migration with POST /orgs/{org}/migrations 2. Wait for the migration to complete (state: "exported") 3. Apply the migration to your target instance 4. Unlock each migrated repository using this action 5. Delete the source repositories if no longer needed

inputs.name: repo_name
inputs.about: The name of the repository to unlock. Must be one of the repositories included in the specified migration.

inputs.name: migration_id

tools.name: Update a label

inputs.name: secret_scanning_push_protection_enabled_for_new_repositories

tools.name: Update an organization variable
tools.description: Updates an existing GitHub Actions organization variable's name, value, or visibility (`all`, `private`, `selected`), requiring `selected_repository_ids` with valid repository IDs if visibility is `selected`.

inputs.name: org

inputs.name: name

inputs.name: value
inputs.about: Optional: The new value for the organization variable. If provided, the variable's value will be updated. If omitted or null, the current value is preserved.

inputs.name: new_name
inputs.about: Optional: The new name for the organization variable. If provided, the variable will be renamed. If omitted or null, the current name is preserved.

inputs.name: visibility
inputs.about: Optional: Specifies the new visibility of the organization variable. Determines which repositories can access this variable: 'all' (all repositories), 'private' (only private repositories), or 'selected' (specific repositories). When set to 'selected', you must also provide `selected_repository_ids`

tools.name: Update an organization webhook
tools.description: Updates an existing organization's webhook configuration, subscribed events, active status, or name. If active status is omitted, the request enables the webhook.

inputs.name: org
inputs.about: The name of the organization. This value is not case-sensitive.

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: Must be passed as 'web' for organization webhooks. This is a fixed value required by the GitHub API.

inputs.name: active
inputs.about: Set to `true` to send notifications, or `false` to disable them.

inputs.name: events
inputs.about: List of events that trigger this webhook. GitHub REPLACES the full event list when this is sent — omit (leave unset) to preserve the existing event subscription. Use `['*']` to subscribe to all events. See GitHub docs for available event types.

inputs.name: hook_id

inputs.name: config__content__type

inputs.name: config__insecure__ssl

tools.name: Update a project

If no owner is specified, the authenticated user is assumed. At least one field to update must be provided.

inputs.name: org

inputs.name: project_number

inputs.name: short_description
inputs.about: A short description for the project (displayed in project cards and listings). If not provided, the description will not be changed.

tools.name: Update a pull request
tools.description: Updates an existing pull request, allowing changes to attributes like title, body, state, base branch, and maintainer modification settings.

When `true`, allows moving the reference to any commit, even if it means rewriting history or

inputs.name: owner

inputs.name: target_commitish

tools.name: Update a release asset

tools.name: Update a repository
